title: Mexico Says Colombia Rejected Its Certified Earthquake Rescue Brigade
detail: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Colombia rejected a Mexican military search-and-rescue brigade despite it holding international certification and having deployed to 98 countries, contradicting Colombian officials' explanation that the team lacked sufficient INSARAG certification. Colombia's Foreign Minister Omar Bula denied any political motivation, saying no country's offer had been excluded, while Colombia's Disaster Management Director reiterated the INSARAG requirement. The dispute — coming after the critical 72-hour survival window had passed — fueled accusations that President de la Espriella's government was screening out rescue offers from left-leaning Latin American governments; Colombia had accepted rescue teams only from the United States, El Salvador, Ecuador, and Israel.

media.caption: Diplomatic friction after Colombia turned away Mexico's rescue brigade

title: De la Espriella Declares Economic Emergency, Launches 'Fondo Milagro' for Reconstruction
detail: President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of economic, social, and ecological emergency, invoking a constitutional measure that grants him authority to issue tax and spending decrees for up to three months without congressional approval, subject to Constitutional Court review of each decree. The move aims to accelerate financing for reconstruction — estimated at roughly COP 20 trillion ($6.4 billion) at the time — in the hardest-hit Chocó, Coffee Region, and Valle del Cauca areas. De la Espriella also launched the 'Fondo Milagro' ('Miracle Fund') to channel domestic and international contributions toward rebuilding hospitals, schools, and infrastructure. The confirmed death toll had reached 273, with 3,824 injured and 377 still missing.

media.caption: De la Espriella announces the 'Fondo Milagro' reconstruction fund
